content.text:
Parsed objects no longer get an own `__proto__` property in any of the cases you listed. The full zod suite passes (3912 tests) and the type check is clean. I didn't commit anything.

- **`z.object` (v4)**: a `__proto__` key declared in the shape stays in `.shape` and survives `.pick`, but parsing skips it in JIT, `jitless` and async modes. It is not written to the output, its schema is never run (so no failures and no defaults), and an own getter on the input isn't invoked. `.strict()` still accepts the key.
- **`fromJSONSchema`**: a `__proto__` property stays in `shape` but is stripped when parsing. `{ role: "x", __proto__: "wrong" }` and `{ role: "x" }` both give `{ role: "x" }`.
- **`z.record` / `z.partialRecord`**: with a finite key set, `__proto__` is skipped whether present or missing, with no key transform or value validation. Loose mode no longer passes it through, and any key whose transformed output is `__proto__` is dropped.
- **`z.intersection` (v3 and v4)**: merged objects have `__proto__` removed, and it isn't merged recursively. The merge also now copies an object that has an own `__proto__` even when both operands are the same object, instead of returning it as-is.
- **Discriminated unions**: no code change needed. They go through the object path, so the output lacks `__proto__` and the existing test now asserts that.

Several existing tests asserted the old "keep `__proto__` as an own property" behaviour, so I rewrote them to assert the new behaviour. Those are in `object.test.ts`, `record.test.ts`, `from-json-schema.test.ts`, `discriminated-unions.test.ts` and the mini `index.test.ts`. I also added intersection tests for v4 and v3.

The main change is in `packages/zod/src/v4/core/schemas.ts`, with the v3 intersection fix in `packages/zod/src/v3/types.ts`.
